name: Pivot with a phase gadget
aliases: Pauli spider removal with a non-Clifford neighbour
summary: An internal Pauli spider connected to an internal spider with arbitrary phase can be removed by pivoting, turning the other spider into a phase gadget.
description:
The [pivot simplification](../pivot/) removes two connected internal spiders that both have a Pauli phase. This variant only requires one of them, $u$, to have a Pauli phase $j\pi$; the other, $v$, may have any phase $\alpha$. After pivoting along $uv$, $u$ is removed, and $v$ becomes a phase gadget: its phase $\alpha$ is moved to a new arity-1 spider, and the remaining phase-free spider is connected to all former neighbours of $u$. The edges between the neighbourhoods are complemented as in the pivot rule; the shared neighbours of $u$ and $v$ get $(j+1)\pi$ added and the neighbours of only $v$ get $j\pi$.

Here the phase gadget is drawn with phase $j\pi$ on its hub and $\alpha$ on its leaf; by π-commutation this is the same as a phase-free hub with leaf $(-1)^j\alpha$, which is how the rule is usually drawn. The rule is used in PyZX's full simplification to remove all internal Pauli spiders, so that the only internal spiders left are non-Clifford spiders and phase gadgets.
parameter_notes: n_u, n_w and n_v are the numbers of neighbours of only u, of both, and of only v (shown for n_u = n_w = n_v = 1). The neighbours may have any number of further legs and edges.
conditions: u and v are internal (not connected to inputs or outputs); u has a Pauli phase jπ.
